policy.resident_food_baseline: 2021-2023 mean FAOSTAT fish and seafood food availability per resident
policy.import_rule: The 2025 retained-import proxy (max of imports minus reported re-exports at each HS heading) multiplied by each year's population/2025 population is a minimum; additional high-cost imports remain open
policy.export_rule: 2025 domestic-export market-weight volume multiplied by each year's population/2025 population is added to final demand
policy.import_variable_cost_role: Screening penalty in million USD/Mt, not a border price. The retained-import pilot with VC=1000 found a maximum FSHFOOD balance dual of 111.38863 discounted in 2024, equivalent to 138.737131 undiscounted; VC=200 remains safely above that observed domestic marginal value.
policy.accounting_capacity_regularization_role: Numerical tie-breaker in million USD/(Mt/year) for the four one-year accounting capacities; prevents arbitrary 999999 capacity results while having immaterial cost.
policy.service_demand_rule: The former fixed SAD values for FSHCAPSERV, FSHAQSERV and FSHPOSTSERV are zero. Fish production now pulls those intermediate services endogenously.
policy.capture_limit: FSHCAPHARV annual activity is capped at 0.023661 Mt/year in 2020-2050 using the included 2020 capture boundary. This is a conservative screening ceiling, not a legal quota or biological stock model.
policy.aquaculture_limit: FSHAQHARV annual activity is capped by the observed/programme envelope: 0.000216925 Mt/year in 2020-2023, rising through the detailed 2024-2028 Table 18 deliverables to 0.00145 Mt/year in 2028, then held constant. This is a programme-based aggregate proxy for feed, land, water, farm-expansion and environmental limits; it does not model those resources separately.
policy.production_floor: No capture or aquaculture minimum is added. The upper limits do not force production; imports remain the feasibility backstop.

population.provider: United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division
population.locator: ISO3_code=FJI; Variant=Medium; Time=2020..2050; TPopulation1July; source values are thousands of people
population.lineage: Exact annual population snapshot already validated for Fiji v2.8.

resident_food.provider: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
resident_food.locator: Area=Fiji; Item=Fish, Seafood; Element=Food supply quantity (kg/capita/yr); Years=2021..2023
resident_food.method: Three-year arithmetic mean of resident food availability. No separate tourism demand is added.
resident_food.quality_note: All three FAOSTAT observations carry flag E (estimated value).

trade.product: UN Comtrade annual HS trade data
trade.locator: period=2025; reporterCode=242 (Fiji); partnerCode=0 (World); flowCode=M for imports and DX for domestic exports; customsCode=C00; motCode=0; HS0301..0309, HS1604 and HS1605; netWgt in kg
trade.method: Four-digit aggregate net weights are used except HS1604 imports, whose aggregate net weight is blank and is reconstructed from available six-digit net weights. The minimum resident-market import proxy is calculated by HS heading as max(total imports minus reported re-exports, zero), then summed. This prevents processing/re-export throughput from displacing Fiji production.
limitations: The HS160431 caviar import has USD 18181.555 of value but no reported weight and is excluded from the mass total.
Trade product weights are treated one-for-one as market-weight fish equivalent; no species, preservation-state or edible-yield conversion is imposed.
Domestic exports use flow DX and therefore exclude separately reported re-exports.

Same-year retained imports are an accounting proxy: re-exports can come from inventories imported in earlier years, so negative code-level differences are floored at zero rather than netted against unrelated fish products.

fisheries_service_calibration.provider: Fiji v2.7 Fisheries source-traceable calibration carried by Fiji v2.8
fisheries_service_calibration.method: 2020 useful-service demands are divided by observed 2020 capture landings, aquaculture harvest and total domestic harvest to create PJ/Mt mass-link coefficients. These are calibration coefficients, not independent 2020 activity requirements in v2.9.

capture_activity_ceiling.locator: Reported 2020-2021 offshore longline catch of 12,661 tonnes plus estimated coastal commercial catch of 11,000 tonnes; retained from the v2.7 evidence ledger.
capture_activity_ceiling.method: The included 23,661 tonne capture boundary is held constant as a conservative full-horizon screening ceiling. It is not presented as a legal quota or a biological stock assessment.

aquaculture_activity_ceiling.provider: Fiji Ministry of Fisheries and Forestry
aquaculture_activity_ceiling.locator: Table 18, Summary of deliverables: December 2024 targets of 300 tonnes tilapia, 15 tonnes giant river prawn and 35 tonnes black tiger shrimp; December 2028 targets of 600, 150 and 700 tonnes, respectively.
aquaculture_activity_ceiling.actuals_locator: National production of 212.83 tonnes tilapia and 4.095 tonnes freshwater prawn, totaling 216.925 tonnes.
aquaculture_activity_ceiling.method: The latest observed total is an upper envelope through 2023. The plan's detailed Table 18 annual deliverables for tilapia, giant river prawn and black tiger shrimp are summed for 2024-2028; the 2028 total is held constant from 2029 through 2050. These are maximum investible programme envelopes, not production demands.

equation_map.mass_links: RYTCM/IAR,OAR -> RateOfUse/RateOfProduction -> EBb4 annual balances for FSHCAPSERV, FSHAQSERV, FSHPOSTSERV, FSHRAW and FSHFOOD
equation_map.capacity: RYT/AF, RT/CAU and RYTTs/CF -> CAa4/CAb1 activity envelopes; one-year zero-cost mass-link capacity is not physical stock

observation_classification.initial_stock: existing v2.8 residual fleet, aquaculture and post-harvest service capacities only
observation_classification.final_demand: population-scaled resident fish availability plus population-scaled 2025 domestic exports
observation_classification.continuing_constraint: population-scaled 2025 import floor; aggregate capture and aquaculture activity ceilings; existing physical asset lives/availability
observation_classification.benchmark_only: capture and aquaculture observations anchor conservative upper envelopes rather than activity requirements; 2020 service demands calibrate PJ/Mt coefficients only

technology_classification.FSHCAPHARV_FSFAQHARV_FSHPOSTPRC: mass-balance conversions with accounting capacity envelopes

design_gate.minimal_candidate: Only RYT/TAU for FSHCAPHARV and FSHAQHARV; 62 annual values; no floor, object, demand or user-defined constraint

diagnostic_history.decision: Set final screening VC to 200, above the observed domestic marginal value but below the provisional 1000.

known_limitations: The normal least-cost solution uses aquaculture for all domestic raw fish and zero capture harvest because no feed, water, land, biological-stock or catch constraint differentiates expansion; the capture/aquaculture split is not calibrated.
Fish is one aggregate market-weight commodity with a one-for-one raw-to-food conversion; species, preservation state, edible yield and processing losses are not represented.
FAOSTAT resident fish availability observations for 2021-2023 are estimated values and are not a dietary recommendation.
The retained-import series is an accounting proxy constructed from same-year trade flows; the import variable cost is a screening penalty, not a border price.
Resident use, retained imports and domestic exports scale exogenously with population; this is not a behavioral trade model.

known_limitations: The constant capture ceiling is a conservative observed-boundary proxy, not a biological stock model or legal quota trajectory.

The aquaculture ceiling is an aggregate programme proxy for feed, suitable land/water, facility expansion and environmental restrictions; those drivers are not separate model commodities or constraints.
The plan contains broader headline goals that differ from its detailed Table 18 deliverables; the implementation uses the more conservative detailed annual table.
Fish remains one aggregate market-weight commodity; species, preservation state, edible yield and processing losses are not represented.
Neither domestic subsector has a minimum-production constraint; a different cost structure could select less domestic production while remaining feasible through imports.
